title: Finite dominant maps to a normal locally Noetherian base are universally open
statement: Let $q:V\to B$ be a finite dominant morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Dominant means that its image is dense. Suppose $B$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and normal, meaning that every local ring of $B$ is an integrally closed domain. Then $q$ is universally open: for every scheme $B\prime$ and every morphism $B\prime\to B$, the projection $V\times_B B\prime\to B\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product] maps open subsets to open subsets.

source.place: Tag 0F32, lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open, finite integral dominant specialization; normal targets are geometrically unibranch by properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-dominant-normal-affine-chart-rings] to $q$. Choose its nonempty affine cover $B=\bigcup_iU_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$, with $q^{-1}(U_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$. The restricted maps are induced by inclusions $A_i\subseteq C_i$ of domains, with $A_i$ Noetherian and normal and $C_i$ finite as an $A_i$-module.

source.place: Tag 030B, lemma-normality-is-local, (3) implies (1), applied to affine chart rings; finite affine inverse images: morphisms.tex Tag 01WH, definition-integral; affine stalks: schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6). This is the affine-chart preparation for more-morphisms.tex Tag 0F32, lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open, finite normal case.

proof.text: For every $i$ choose finite module generators of $C_i$ over $A_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-domain-polynomial-extension-data] to this inclusion and these generators. For every $n\ge0$ it gives an inclusion of domains $A_n=A_i[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\subseteq C_n=C_i[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, where $A_n$ is normal and Noetherian and $C_n$ is integral and finitely presented over $A_n$, with the same constant module generators.

source.place: Tag 030A, lemma-polynomial-domain-normal; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation (3); Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral. The coefficientwise map and unchanged module generators are the elementary polynomial calculation in the finite affine specialization of more-morphisms.tex Tag 0F32, lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open.

proof.text: We now have an inclusion of domains $A_n\subseteq C_n$, with $A_n$ normal and $C_n$ integral over it. The going-down theorem supplies, for every prime chain $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p\prime$ in $A_n$ and every prime $\mathfrak q\prime$ of $C_n$ above $\mathfrak p\prime$, a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q\prime$ above $\mathfrak p$. Since $C_n$ is finitely presented over $A_n$, the finitely-presented going-down openness criterion shows that $\operatorname{Spec}(C_n)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_n)$ is open. This holds for every $n\geq0$ and every chart $i$.

source.place: Tag 00H8, proposition-going-down-normal-integral, then Tag 00I1, proposition-fppf-open, second assertion

proof.text: For each $i$, apply the polynomial test to $A_i\to C_i$, using the openness established for every $n$ in step 3. It gives universal openness of $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$, so all its base changes by arbitrary schemes are open. In particular the auxiliary base schemes need not remain normal, reduced, or locally Noetherian.

Let $h:B\prime\to B$ be any scheme morphism and $p:V\times_B B\prime\to B\prime$ its projection. The inverse images $U_i\prime=h^{-1}(U_i)$ form an open cover of $B\prime$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $p^{-1}(U_i\prime)\to U_i\prime$ with the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ along $U_i\prime\to U_i$; the projections agree because both satisfy the same two projection equations. By step 4 this restricted map is open. For any open $O\subseteq V\times_B B\prime$, the equality $p(O)\cap U_i\prime=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i\prime)}(O\cap p^{-1}(U_i\prime))$ shows that $p(O)$ is open on every member of an open cover, hence open. This proves universal openness of $q$.
